coverage_note: West Virginia has no public-sector collective bargaining statute. A 2021 statute (W. Va. Code 18-5-45a, in the education chapter) declares that public employees have no right to bargain collectively and that public-employee strikes are unlawful. The Workplace Freedom Act (21-5G) bars compulsory dues or fees.

governing_statute.value: None authorizing bargaining. W. Va. Code 18-5-45a(a)(2) declares that public employees have no right, statutory or otherwise, to collective bargaining, mediation or arbitration
governing_statute.quote: (2) Public employees in West Virginia have no right, statutory or otherwise, to engage in collective bargaining, mediation, or arbitration, and any work stoppage or strike by public employees is hereby declared to be unlawful.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. The Workplace Freedom Act bars requiring payment of dues or fees to a labor organization as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: A person may not be required, as a condition or continuation of employment, to: (1) Become or remain a member of a labor organization; (2) Pay any dues, fees, assessments or other similar charges, however denominated, of any kind or amount to any labor organization;
